name: IT University of Copenhagen
about: ITU was founded in 1999, has about 2,900 students, and is built around a single subject: information technology and what it does to people, business and society. Everything happens in one building in Ørestad in southern Copenhagen, so it feels much more like a large department than a campus university. All four bachelor's degrees have restricted admission and published GPA cut-offs, and only two of them are taught in English.

languageOfInstruction.note: ITU offers four bachelor's degrees but only two are taught in English. BSc Software Development is taught in Danish and requires Danish A; BSc Digital Design and Interactive Technologies is mainly Danish (only the second year is taught entirely in English) and also requires Danish A. Neither is listed here.

subjects.subject: Mathematics
subjects.text: ITU accepts a VUC course, the University of Amsterdam's online Mathematics B (it counts as Mathematics A) or an International A level in Mathematics at C or better.

subjects.subject: Danish
subjects.text: ITU: "You complete a supplementary course in Danish level A. In Denmark, supplementary courses are offered by VUC."

levelRaise.timing: With conditional admission (fee-exempt applicants only) enrolment must be documented by 5 July, 12:00, and the pass by 1 September.

groups.timing: Conditional admission is for fee-exempt applicants only, so without fee exemption the course has to be passed before you are admitted.
groups.multiple: Without fee exemption there is no conditional admission, so every course has to be passed before you are admitted.

sources.title: ITU names its routes to Mathematics A (VUC, the University of Amsterdam's online courses, an International A level) and to Danish A (a VUC supplementary course); conditional admission, with enrolment documented by 5 July and the pass by 1 September, is only for applicants exempt from tuition fees.

notes: ITU offers four bachelor's degrees but only two are taught in English. BSc Software Development is taught in Danish and requires Danish A; BSc Digital Design and Interactive Technologies is mainly Danish (only the second year is taught entirely in English) and also requires Danish A. Neither is listed here.

Read the Danish requirement carefully: BSc Global Business Informatics is taught in English but still demands Danish at A level as a passed subject, so in practice it is open only to applicants who have studied Danish. ITU's own BSc overview page says "only the programme in Data Science is open to international students".
BSc Data Science is the one ITU degree an IB student from outside Denmark can realistically enter — 73 per cent of the students admitted in 2026 were international.
ITU has a summer intake only; there is no February start at bachelor's level.

From the 2027 admission round ITU requires an overall GPA of at least 6.0 on the Danish 7-point scale for BSc Software Development. Check whether a similar floor has been added to the English-taught degrees before applying.

Everything happens in one building in Ørestad in southern Copenhagen, so it feels much more like a large department than a campus university. All four bachelor's degrees have restricted admission and published GPA cut-offs, and only two of them are taught in English.

programmes.name: Data Science
programmes.about: Three years of programming, mathematics, statistics and machine learning, taught with a lot of project work and an eye on what the data actually means for people. You do not need to have coded before. Graduates go into data science, machine learning engineering and analytics roles in finance, health, journalism and public planning.

admission.capacityNote: 100 study places in 2026; 595 applicants, of whom 417 applied in quota 2.

selection.description: A motivational cover letter is recommended for quota 2 applicants.

requirements.label: A qualifying upper-secondary examination

officialWording.text: International Baccalaureate (IB) med IB-Course Result på mindst 18 point sidestilles med en gymnasial eksamen, hvis ansøgeren har opnået mindst karakteren 3 i hvert af de 6 fag, der indgår i IB-forløbet. Endvidere skal ansøgeren have gennemført enkeltfag på gymnasialt niveau svarende til overbygning, jf. reglerne om overbygning i højere forberedelseseksamen (hf-eksamen) i lov om gymnasiale uddannelser.

requirements.alternativeRoute: It does not close this one to you. The Danish Agency treats DP Course Results of at least 18 points, with at least grade 3 in all six subjects and at least three of them at HL, as equivalent to a qualifying examination for a Danish university bachelor once you have added two successive raises in the level of upper-secondary subjects, at least one of them to A level, taken as hf-enkeltfag or as a self-study candidate. If you already hold an A-level subject other than Danish, two raises to B level are enough. Retaking to be awarded the full IB Diploma is the other published route.
requirements.note: The rule is national rather than this university's: the Danish Agency for Higher Education and Science sets which examinations are adgangsgivende, and every Danish institution applies the same one. Two things about it are easy to get wrong. GSK (gymnasial supplering) cannot be used for this — GSK raises a subject level for someone who already holds a qualifying examination, so it meets a specific subject requirement but never raises the level of the examination itself. And the average used in quota 1 is the one from the first qualifying examination, so a Course Results holder who supplements or retakes is still converted on the original Course Results result.

sources.title: DP Course Results (formerly the IB Certificate) of at least 18 points, with at least grade 3 in all six subjects and at least three subjects at HL, are a qualifying examination in Denmark on the same terms as a two-year hf without overbygning: they give access to erhvervsakademi- and professionsbachelor programmes through quota 1 and quota 2, and to a university bachelor only after two successive raises of upper-secondary subject level, at least one to A level, taken as hf-enkeltfag. Course Results under 18 points, or containing any subject at grade 1 or 2, are not a qualifying examination at all. A full IB Diploma of 24 points or more gives access to every higher education programme in Denmark.
sources.quote: IB-elever uden IB Diploma, men med mindst 18 point (Diploma Programme (DP) Course Results), har adgang til videregående uddannelser i Danmark på lige vilkår med ansøgere med den 2-årige hf-eksamen uden overbygning. Det kræver, at alle 6 IB-fag (3 HL-fag og 3 SL- eller 4 HL-fag og 2 SL-fag) er bestået med mindst karakteren 3. Det betyder, at de har adgang til at søge optagelse på erhvervsakademi- og professionsbacheloruddannelser gennem kvote 1 og 2. Ansøgere med et Diploma Programme (DP) Course Results på mindst 18 point og mindst karakteren 3 i alle fag kan derudover få adgang til en universitetsbacheloruddannelse gennem kvote 1 og 2 ved enten at supplere med enkeltfag efter samme regler som hf’erne eller tage deres IB-eksamen om for at få et IB Diploma – Retake.

alternativeRouteSummary.short: Course Results of 18+ points (grade 3 in all six, three at HL) count once you raise two subjects a level, one of them to A level. Or retake for the Diploma.

programmes.name: Global Business Informatics

sources.title: ITU – BSc in Global Business Informatics

programmes.about: A degree about how organisations actually use digital technology — AI, business analytics and digital transformation — rather than about building the technology itself. It is taught in English, but be warned: you must also have passed Danish at A level, so it is realistically only open to applicants who have Danish at A level — from a Danish gymnasium, or Danish A in the IB. Going to school in Denmark is not enough on its own.

admission.capacityNote: 71 study places in 2026; 92 per cent of those admitted had Danish qualifications.
